newsitem.title: USA: Walgreen posts record results, sees 280 new stores in 1998. [CORRECTED 20:29 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Walgreen posts record results, sees 280 new stores in 1998. [CORRECTED 20:29 GMT]

text.p: Walgreen Co., reporting record third-quarter results, said Monday it expects to open 280 new drugstores in 1998 and could add as many as a store a day in 1999.

Walgreen, the nation's largest drugstore chain, also said it has agreed to sell its electronic prescription network, Pre-Scribe, to ProxyMed, Inc., a healthcare information technology company, for undisclosed terms.
The Pre-Scribe network allows physicians to fill prescriptions on computers linked to local pharmacies.

Walgreen said it opened 151 new stores from September through May and is on course to add 230 new outlets in 1997. Of the new stores, 43 were relocations of existing stores, and that ratio is expected to be about the same in 1998, a Walgreen spokesman said.
Walgreens, based in Deerfield, Ill., operates 2,289 drugstores in 34 states and Puerto Rico, up from 2,149 a year ago.

Walgreen said it earned $108.1 million, or 44 cents a share, for the third quarter ended May 31, compared with $91.6 million, or 37 cents a share, a year ago. Revenues grew 13.9 percent to $3.4 billion from almost $3 billion (corrects from million).
Walgreen Chairman Charles Walgreen III said the company's results reflect its aggressive growth strategy, investment of more than $400 million in 1997 and strong cost controls.
Walgreen said it expects to post its 23rd consecutive year of record results in fiscal 1997.
The company earned $371.7 million, or $1.50 a share, on sales of $11.8 billion in fiscal 1996, which ended Aug. 31.
Walgreen's stock rose $1.25 to $52.06 on the New York Stock Exchange in late morning trading.
